newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Airways Corp withdraws application to NZCC.
newsitem.headline: Airways Corp withdraws application to NZCC.

text.p: Airways Corporation of New Zealand said on Friday it had withdrawn an application to the Commerce Commission seeking approval for a timetable to move to location-specific pricing for aerodrome services.

The application was lodged with the commission on November 18, 1996. Earlier in February a draft determination from the commission ruled against approving the application, arguing the proposed arrangements would allow Airways to delay the introduction of competition for air traffic control services.
A final decision was due by the end of March, but will now no longer be issued, the commission said on Friday.

The Commerce Commission received a complaint in August alleging Airways' existing network pricing for aerodrome services was anti-competitive. Airways told the commission it was preparing to move to location-specific pricing on a national basis.
Airways' group commercial manager Stuart Wilson said the withdrawal of the application meant the change to location-specific pricing may happen sooner than Airways had proposed.
"Airways will have to move to location-specific pricing as soon as possible, otherwise there is a serious risk that we may be in breach of the Commerce Act," Wilson said.
"We support the concept of competition and we are confident that we can find a mechanism that will allow competition to occur in an efficient manner."
